summary: This 3-page paper presents a two-layer, zero-floating-point verification stack motivated by geometric primitives in OpenAI's November 24, 2026 preprint on Euclidean geometry in Strassen's asymptotic spectrum of tensors [1]. Layer 1 (lean/AsymptoticSpectrumGeometry.lean, Lean 4.35.0, 18 theorems, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice) proves exact 2D integer Euclidean laws (Euclid's parametrization, translation/homogeneity invariance, Lagrange's 2D Cauchy-Schwarz, rational-length triangle inequality, segment-restricted collinear zero-excess, and 2D scaled-rotation isometry/contraction) plus elementary integer/list projections. Layer 2 (SPEC-GEOM-CERT-1.0, pure-stdlib Python Fraction) audits exact-Q certificates across four modes (strict CCW convex polygons with W = P/2, collinear vs. exterior triangle gaps, 2D similarity contractions, and finite arithmetic barrier witnesses), replaying 16 certificates in 0.071-0.313 ms, cross-checking W = P/2 against 4096-angle Cauchy-Crofton integration, and rejecting 58/58 adversarial forgeries. All visible algebraic statements, witnesses, and figures are consistent and honestly scoped; main limitations are modest mathematical novelty, trivial scalar/list content in Theorems 7-11 and 14-18, and no formal Lean-to-Python soundness bridge.
weaknesses: Ten of the 18 Lean theorems (Theorems 7-11 and 14-18) are one-line scalar or list-sum inequalities (e.g., h < 2h, integer distributivity, 2^k < 2^{k+1}, and linear list-sum domination d_i <= C e_i => sum d_i <= C sum e_i) whose theorem identifiers (such as matmul_triangle_sharing_bound, strassen_semiring_distributivity, cube_exclusion_dim_jump, port_graph_quadratic_domination, and diagonal_price_contradiction) sound far more substantial than their mathematical content, even though Section 1 and Theorem 2.1(4) acknowledge their elementary nature.

There is no formal verification bridge between Layer 1 (Lean 4 over Z) and Layer 2 (Python Fraction over Q): Lean 4 does not prove the soundness of SPEC-GEOM-CERT-1.0, does not formalize the Mode 1 CCW convexity-to-simple-polygon theorem, and does not prove Cauchy's planar mean-width identity W(S) = P/2 (which relies on [2] and numerical 4096-angle integration).

Mode 4 (strassen_borrowed_wire_barrier_exact) audits decoupled synthetic scalar/list inequalities on manually supplied rationals (e.g., h_I, e_1, e_2, prem, h_err, margin) rather than verifying any actual tensor rank, circuit, or port-graph construction.
Mode 1 global strict CCW half-plane check is O(m^2) and rules out polygons with three collinear boundary vertices, restricting certified polygons to strictly convex rational-edge-length polygons.
This PDF-only assessment cannot independently execute the Lean 4.35.0 kernel, Python verification scripts, or 58-case adversarial suite reported from the author's repository.
